text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) meeting in Vienna ON Friday to discuss report on Yugoslav local elections. Yugoslav government seeks more time to give its official answer to report.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno supporters continue protests in Belgrade's central square vowing to persevere until election results are reinstated.
- Serbian Orthodox Church condemns authorities over situation in Serbia following local elections.
- Serbs can be satisfied with the level of autonomy of Bosnian Serb republic, says Momcilo Krajisnik, Serb representataive in collective Bosnian presidency.

- Serbian textile and leather industries are in very difficult situation -- their exports in 1996 stood at only $140 million as compared to $1.1 billion in 1991, says Gradimir Cvetkovic of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce.
- Montenegro offers its aid, support and understanding to Serbia in democratically overcoming its problems, says Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic.
- Following Yugoslav federal government decision, taxi drivers will be able to import cars with only four percent customs duty.
- Serbia expects to earn $120 million from tourism in 1997 as against $40 million earned last year, says Serbian Tourism Minister Radisav Stankovic.
- Priorities of Yugoslavia's 1997 economic policy are maintaining stability of prices and foreign-currency exchange rate through market measures, says federal government.

- Serbian government will allow foreign credits of up to 140 million German marks to pharmaceutical producers as step to resolve debts in health sector, says Serbian Health Minister Leposava Milicevic.
